title: List of bugged spells
html:
This list aims to catalogue spells which do not function as would be expected based on their tooltips, or which have other problems - or missing information - in their description, function, or location. This list is unlikely to be comprehensive as it is likely there are many issues with spells of which we are unaware.

As this list deals with problems that have a high likelihood of being changed in patches and hotfixes, it is likely that entries will be incorrect following an update.

All entries are currently correct as of Hotfix 33.

Spells

More...
Name Bugs
 Animate Dead: Ghoul
  • Due to a coding error, ghouls summoned by a Necromancy School wizard with  Undead Thralls: Better Summons, while affected by  Rejuvenating Miasma, fail to spawn unless a corpse is targeted, wasting the spell slot used to cast Animate Dead.
 Animate Dead: Zombie Battalion
  • Due to a coding error, zombies summoned by a Necromancy School wizard with  Undead Thralls: Better Summons, while affected by  Rejuvenating Miasma, fail to spawn unless a corpse is targeted, wasting the spell slot used to cast Animate Dead.
 Arabella's Shadow Entangle
  • Although this spell's tooltip states it applies  Weavebound Vines until long rest, it behaves identically to  Entangle.
 Arcane Critical
  • While the tooltip says Arcane Critical improves your critical hit threshold by 2, it actually only improves it by 1.
 Armour of Agathys
  • When upcast to either spell slot level 3 or 4, the tooltip description incorrectly references the condition applied via the spell slot level 1 version.
 Banishing Smite
  • Banishing Smite (Ranged) cast at level 6 incorrectly spends a level 5 spell slot.
 Banishment
  • Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times, requiring a saving throw for each time they were selected.
 Bear's Endurance
  • The temporary hit points lack a StackPriority and as such are overridden by any other source of temporary hit points, even if the new source is of a lesser value.
 Blade Barrier
  • The DC for this spell save does not function properly:
    • The initial spell save DC for damage caused by casting and entering the wall is fixed at 15.
    • The DC for starting a turn inside the wall is fixed at 3.
    • The DC for starting a turn near the wall is fixed at 10.
 Blight
  • This spell lacks an IsHarmful spell flag, and as such is able to target creatures affected by  Sanctuary.
  • When cast at spell slot level 4 against a non-plant enemy that fails the saving throw, Blight incorrectly deals non-magical damage.
 Blinding Smite
  • All spell slot versions of this action change attack animations in Honour mode due to an override in the code.
 Blindness
  • Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times, requiring a saving throw for each time they are selected.
 Blink
  • Despite purposely ignoring the functor which breaks Concentration, a StatusGroup error still breaks Concentration when vanishing.
  • When vanishing into the Ethereal Plane, equipped items are temporarily disabled. This causes item technical statuses that include OnRemoveFunctors (such as those used by Markoheshkir) to trigger, removing any effects provided by those items.
 Bone-shaking Thunder
  • The version of Destructive Wave granted by this condition still displays the individual variant spells ( Destructive Wave: Necrotic/ Destructive Wave: Radiant) as costing a  Level 5 Spell Slot. Though no actual spell slot cost is incurred by the caster, these variants will still activate effects which trigger when spending spell slots.
 Booming Blade
  • Though it is not displayed in its description, Booming Blade can be cast while  Silenced.
  • This cantrip is not correctly classified as a ⁠Thunder spell so it does not work with the following effects:
    •  Bone-shaking Thunder
    •  Destructive Wrath
    •  Elemental Adept: Thunder
    •  Heart of the Storm: Thunder
    •  Necklace of Elemental Augmentation
    •  Ring of Absolute Force
    •  Prophecy: Thunderous Applause
  • Some other elemental effects are implemented differently and work with the ⁠Thunder damage Booming Blade receives at level 5. These effects include:
    •  Boots of Elemental Momentum
    •  Gloves of Belligerent Skies
    •  Hat of Storm Scion's Power
    •  Ring of Elemental Infusion
      • Due to an additional bug, these items do not work in Honour mode unless the weapon itself deals elemental damage (e.g., from  Elemental Weapon or any innate elemental damage bonus).
 Boon of Servitude
  • The tooltip of the action incorrectly states Boon of Servitude heals for 2~83⁠⁠Hit Points, while that of the condition itself incorrectly states it heals for 2~81⁠⁠Hit Points.
 Brand the Weak
  • Brand the Weak does not display that it costs a Bonus Action on its spell container.
 Branding Smite
  • Branding Smite cast with a  Level 4 Spell Slot incorrectly lists tooltip damage using the  Level 2 Spell Slot of the spell.
  • The spell container for Branding Smite does not correctly display the current spell slot level for Warlocks.
  • This spell lacks a restriction against targeting items, and due to the small radius and its target limit of 1 it is possible to target a creature but have  Branding Smite applied to an item within the radius.
 Calm Emotions
  • Despite the description, there are no Humanoid-only targeting restrictions.
 Chain Lightning
  • This spell lacks an IsHarmful spell flag, and as such is able to target creatures affected by  Sanctuary.
 Cloudkill
  • If upcast to level 6, Cloudkill creates an invisible cloud due to the surface lacking an attached particle effect.
    • NPCs will not automatically leave this cloud, as its surface ID is missing from character PathInfluence.
  • The cloud lasts for 10 turns starting from the last time it was recast instead of starting from the initial cast. This often leads to a situation where the caster no longer has the ability to recast Cloudkill, but both the Concentration effect and the cloud persist for longer than they would otherwise be expected to.
 Conjure Barrage: Melee Weapon
  • Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    •  Great Weapon Master: All In
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Prepare
    •  Wrath
 Conjure Barrage: Ranged Weapon
  • Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    • Gloves of Archery
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Sharpshooter: All In
    • Titanstring Bow
 Conjure Shadow Lantern Wraith
  • The ingame tooltip states "The target must be a Medium or Small corpse", but a corpse is not required; the spell conjures a creature from within the lantern.
  • Despite this spell's name, the creature summoned is a  Shadow, not the more powerful  Wraith. It is unable to climb surfaces such as ladders and knotted roots, and is unable to  Jump,  Fly, or  Warp, meaning it may be unable to follow the party to certain areas. Regrouping is possible by entering a new area or using Waypoints.
 Counterspell
  • When attempting to Counterspell a spell of a higher level, the Counterspell caster's  Intelligence modifier is used instead of their spellcasting ability modifier as the tooltip states.'"`UNIQ--ref-00000031-QINU`"'
  • Arcane Ward can only be fed up to 3 charges, regardless of spell Level used, due to how an additional hidden Counterspell is cast based on success/failure.
 Crusader's Mantle
  • Crusader's Mantle also affects neutral creatures, not just allied characters.
 Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War
  • Despite originating from a spell, damage from this spell is dealt as if from a non-magical source.
 Danse Macabre
  • The tooltip incorrectly states it costs a  Level 5 Spell Slot.
 Daylight
  • Although exposing Duergar, Drow and other NPCs to either variant of this spell does trigger  Sunlight Sensitivity, it will not show any status effect for the player to see (e.g., as a passive or condition on their character sheets, if examined), yet one can check the combat logs to see the effects of  Disadvantage being applied.
  • Although the in-game description of the enchant item variant lists a 20-turn limit, if applied to a character, the effect will be applied to their held main-hand weapon until long rest and will persist even if the caster is no longer in the active party.
 Daylight: Enchant Item
  • Although the in-game descriptions of both this spell and the spell container list a 20-turn limit for this variant, if applied to a character, the effect will be applied to their held main-hand weapon until long rest and will persist even if the caster is no longer in the active party.
  • Although exposing Duergar, Drow and other NPCs to light within range from this spell does trigger  Sunlight Sensitivity, it will not show any status effect for the player to see (e.g., as a passive or condition on their character sheets, if examined), yet one can check the combat logs to see the effects of  Disadvantage being applied.
  • This spell cannot be cast on a non-allied creature due to a coding mistake, which would otherwise have required them to make a  Dexterity saving throw with DC equal to the caster's spell save DC to avoid the effect.
 Daylight: Sphere
  • Although exposing Duergar, Drow and other NPCs to light within radius from spell does trigger  Sunlight Sensitivity, it will not show any status effect for the player to see (e.g., as a passive or condition on their character sheets, if examined), yet one can check the combat logs to see the effects of  Disadvantage being applied.
 Death Ward
  • Death Ward uses  Survival Instinct as a Parent condition, and as such inherits the Action point restoration it possesses. This can be exploited by a character casting Death Ward on themselves, allowing them to continuously regenerate Action points so long as they are able to both down themselves and recast Death Ward multiple times per turn.
 Destructive Wave
  • This spell is classified as a ⁠Radiant or ⁠Necrotic spell depending on the variant rather than a ⁠Thunder spell. This means it will not work with Tempest Domain's  Destructive Wrath or  Bone-shaking Thunder's bonus damage.
 Detect Thoughts
  • Despite the tooltip saying this spell uses either Intelligence or Wisdom, only the creature’s Intelligence is used, even if its Wisdom is higher; this is likely an oversight.
 Dirty Trick: Vicious Mockery
  • When the target fails the saving throw, the combat log erroneously states that the caster failed the saving throw.
 Disguise Self
  • If a companion or hireling is disguised while at camp, they will remain where they were last placed when another companion or player character is selected, rather than automatically moving back to their tent, until they are moved again or a long rest is taken. This can be useful when seeking to apply conditions or spells with a limited radius, such as  Aid.
    • This bug does not apply to  Jaheira if she herself is bugged and recruited to the party.
  • Disguise Self disables effects which require the Brand of the Absolute to trigger, such as  Gloves of Power.
  • As of Patch 5, Hotfix 17, it is possible to give the caster racial equipment bonuses for longer than intended by using the  Mask of the Shapeshifter, taking the mask off, and long resting without removing the disguise. On waking up, the disguise will be gone, but the racial bonuses on the equipment will still affect the character. This only works for racial equipment bonuses, not racial dialogue options.
  • If the player character is disguised as a githyanki when talking to  Shadowheart for the first time on the beach at the start of Act One they are awarded an extra 30 xp.
  • Dialogue options to kiss romanced companions are unavailable while they are disguised.
  • While hirelings are disguised, they cannot be spoken with.
  • While disguised, if companions are slated to speak during cut-scenes, they might not be seen or heard, though if they are not their lines can still be read on-screen.
 Dispel Evil And Good
  • Despite the description, this spell lacks any function versus Aberrations.
 Dispel Evil And Good: Break Enchantment
  • This spell removes  Frightened only, rather than any effect from the Frightened status group.
 Disrobing Blinkstep
  • Sorcerers are able to twin-cast disrobing blinkstep which allows them to select two teleportation positions. It is unclear if this has any effect aside from the caster teleporting to the second position.
 Dominate Person
  • The level 10 Enchantment Wizard feature  Split Enchantment allows the caster to target two humanoids with this spell, but only dominates one - even with failed saves - as the second instance of domination ends the effect of the first.
 Drunken Inhale
  • The tooltip says that targets still take half damage on a successful save, but they actually take (2d8)/2Poison damage which is a quarter of the normal damage.
 Elemental Age
  • Casting Elemental Age while standing on top of weapons that are on the ground will enchant both the Flail of Ages and the weapons at the same time.
  • The description states that "The blade can be unequipped and equipped again, but has to stay on the spellcaster's person." but this is simply text inherited from the parent spell Shout_FlameBlade and has no actual function.
 Elemental Retort
  •  Silence does not prevent Lorroakan from casting this spell despite technically requiring a verbal component.
  • This reaction can trigger off any action that targets Lorroakan, not just ones that damage him as the tooltip claims.
 Enhance Ability
  • When selected as a bonus to an ability check in dialogue, this spell may be[verify] cast at the highest available level; up-casting has no effect.
  • Unlike other concentration spells, spellcasters who require preparation can maintain concentration on this spell after removing it from their prepared spells list.[verify]
 Enlarge
  • Despite not being mentioned in the condition description, unarmed attacks, but not those made while transformed by Wild Shape, are affected by Enlarge.
 Enlarge (Duergar)
  • Despite not being mentioned in the description, unarmed attacks, but not those made while transformed by Wild Shape, are affected by Enlarge.
 Ensnaring Strike (Ranged)
  • When upcast to level 4, Ensnaring Strike (Ranged) erroneously costs an  Action +  Level 4 Spell Slot on use and a  Bonus Action +  Level 1 Spell Slot on hit.
 Entangle
  • Entangle has TargetConditions of not Grounded(), which means it cannot be targeted against creatures that have the Grounded attribute (such  Ketheric Thorm with  Reaper's Rigidity). Despite this restriction, Entangle does affect creatures that have the Grounded attribute (without any change in functionality), and can be cast against such creatures by indirectly targeting them within the AoE circle.
 Expeditious Retreat
  • Expeditious Retreat lacks the second-level of Dash-stacking functionality found on other Dash abilities.
  • Expeditious Retreat lacks the Dash SpellCategory, and will not trigger passives found on items such as  Linebreaker Boots or  The Speedy Lightfeet.
    • The subsequently granted  Dash (bonus action) correctly triggers these passives.
 Fanatic Retaliation
  • Despite having the HasVerbalComponent flag, this reaction can be cast while silenced.
 Fire Shield
  • Contrary to the description, neither  Fire Shield: Warm nor  Fire Shield: Chill applies any gameplay light effect to the affected creature.
 Flame Blade
  • A permanent Flame Blade can be obtained by having a druid hireling such as  Danton cast this spell, immediately recalling their soul, and hiring them again. A Flame Blade created this way loses its technical FLAME_BLADE status which causes it to revert to a normal melee weapon.
    • Attacks count as normal melee weapon attacks rather than melee spell attacks.
    • It uses the normal melee attack modifier for the attack roll and damage. Normally this is Strength, but features like  Pact of the Blade and  Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks can change this.
    • It is no longer bound to the summoner and can be holstered, thrown, and transferred to party members.
    • It no longer interacts with the  Gloves of Battlemage's Power or  Pyroquickness Hat.
    • It no longer emits light.
    • It loses the flaming visual effect.
 Flaming Sphere
  • The DC for both Ram attack and Ablaze is always calculated using the caster's Wisdom modifier, even for wizards.
 Flesh to Gold
  • Despite the description stating the effect lasts 'until the spell ends,' petrification from this spell is indeed permanent until the target is cured by  Basilisk Oil or a spell such as  Greater Restoration.
  • Flesh to Gold incorrectly uses the icon from Flesh to Stone, which it uses as a parent spell.
  • Despite requiring Concentration to cast, Flesh to Gold's concentration immediately ends once the target has progressed to Flesh to Gold: Stage 2 and is no longer required afterwards.
  • Through use of a khn function named HasFleshToSToneCheck(), Flesh to Stone and Flesh to Gold should be uncastable on a target which is already afflicted with either of these two spells. However, this function only includes checks for the Flesh to Stone conditions, and as such Flesh to Stone is castable on a creature already afflicted with Flesh to Gold.
 Flesh to Stone
  • Despite the description stating the effect is 'temporary,' petrification from this spell is indeed permanent until the target is cured by Basilisk Oil or a spell such as  Greater Restoration.
  • Through use of a khn function named HasFleshToSToneCheck(), Flesh to Stone and  Flesh to Gold should not be castable on a target which is already afflicted with either of these two spells. However, this function only includes checks for the Flesh to Stone conditions, and as such Flesh to Stone can be cast on a creature already afflicted with Flesh to Gold.
 Fog Cloud
  • The radius of Fog Cloud does not consistently increase by 2 m (7 ft) for each spell slot level cast above the 1st. Instead, the following occurs:
    • Spell slot 1 to spell slot 2 increases the radius by 1.5 m (5 ft).
    • Spell slot 2 to spell slot 3 increases the radius by 2 m (7 ft).
    • Spell slot 3 to spell slot 4 increases the radius by 2 m (7 ft).
    • Spell slot 4 to spell slot 5 increases the radius by 0.5 m (2 ft).
    • Spell slot 5 to spell slot 6 increases the radius by 1.5 m (5 ft).
  • The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 1 is 4 m (13 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 4.5 m (15 ft).
  • The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 5 is 12 m (40 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 10.5 m (35 ft).
  • The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 6 is 14 m (47 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 12 m (40 ft).
Forced Teleportation Forced Teleportation
  • The tooltip of this spell erroneously states that it deals 3d8⁠⁠Necrotic damage, but it has no associated attack or damage roll. It only serves to mark Astarion as a target during the ritual, after which he is trapped and teleported to his ritual circle.
 Freedom of Movement
  • Despite the description, there is no differentiation between magical and non-magical sources of  Paralysed or  Restrained (all are removed/prevented), nor is there any function which allows an affected creature to spend 1.5 m (5 ft) of Movement to free itself from any effects.
  • Ineffective against  Maimed.
 Ghoulish Touch
  • Contrary to the tooltip, elves and undead can be paralysed.
 Githyanki Psionics: Jump
  • This spell has a Ritual tag on the tooltip despite being usable only once per Long Rest.
 Globe of Invulnerability
  • Casting this on or near camp followers and inactive party members can cause them to lose attitude or become hostile, despite it being a beneficial effect.
  • Casting  Spirit Guardians while inside a globe consumes both action and spell slot without actually casting the spell.
 Glyph of Warding: Cold
  • If cast on a wet surface, the DC to avoid  Prone from the  Ice surface created by this spell is based of the entity which created the wet surface instead of the caster.
    • If a druid casts  Create Water and a wizard casts  Glyph of Warding: Cold, the DC to avoid Ice's Prone will be: 8 + druid INT modifier + druid proficiency + druid equipment bonus, instead of 8 + wizard INT Modifier + wizard proficiency + wizard equipment bonus.
    • This formula only works if the water first had contact with the enemies (e.g., casting Create Water on top of NPCs), if cast/thrown to the ground and then frozen by this spell, the Prone DC will have a default value of 12.
 Grant Flight
  • Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times for no additional effect.
 Grave Repulsion
  • The tooltip incorrectly states targets are pushed back 15 m / 50 ft instead of 8 m / 27 ft.
 Guardian of Faith
  • Code exists for each Guardian to display the heraldry of the summoner's deity on its shield, but due to an incorrect context check it fails to display.
 Hail of Thorns
  • Since the primary roll of this ability is not a weapon attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    •  Gloves of Archery
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Sharpshooter: All In
    •  Titanstring Bow
  • If the target fails the initial saving throw, the attack roll always succeeds.
 Harm
  • On a failed saving throw, Harm reduces the target's maximum hit points by 14d6 but does not actually inflict any ⁠Necrotic damage. This means that it does not trigger damage riders or other effects which require a damage source. Further, the effective damage dealt (through the reduction in maximum hit points) is reduced by the amount of hit points the target was already missing, potentially to zero.
    • On a successful saving throw, Harm deals 14d6 / 2⁠⁠Necrotic damage as expected.
  • Creatures immune to disease receive no damage if they fail their save, but still take half damage if they succeed.
 Heat Metal
  • Due to a coding error, the condition which provides Disadvantage to the target (applied after a successful saving throw) is removed if another unrelated condition is removed from the target.
    • This particular bug only affects the level 2 version of this spell.
  • Due to a coding error, the condition which provides Disadvantage to the target is not automatically removed if the Heat Metal spell is ended early.
    • This particular bug affects all levels of this spell.
  • Heat Metal cast at level 4 deals only 2d8⁠⁠Fire, and its tooltip does not display the damage which Reapply Heat Metal deals.
    • It additionally lacks several other functors found in other levels of this spell.
    • Reapply Heat Metal cast at level 4 correctly deals 4d8⁠⁠Fire.
  • Reapply Heat Metal cast at levels 5 and 6 incorrectly displays its tooltip damage as the level 3 version.
 Hellflame Cleave
  • Despite the tooltip saying that Hellfire ignores resistances and immunities, it does not.
  • Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    •  Great Weapon Master: All In
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Prepare
    •  Wrath
 Hellish Rebuke
  • When upcast to spell slot level 5 or 6, the damage from Hellish Rebuke is reduced by  Evasion whereas the lower spell slot versions are not.
  • There are multiple bugs involving Hellish Rebuke and the combat log:
    • When upcast to spell slot level 3 or 4, Hellish Rebuke's damage tooltip states it only deals
      2d10 (2~20) ⁠Fire
      damage. The actual damage dealt is the correct amount for the spell slot level used.
    • When upcast to spell slot level 5 or 6, Hellish Rebuke's description states it only deals
      2d10 (2~20) ⁠Fire
      damage. The actual damage dealt is the correct amount for the spell slot level used.
 Hex
  • If a creature has Hex applied, and lands a Critical Hit against the caster that triggers any "on hit / damage" abilities to damage the hexed creature, the damage of  Hex is doubled along with the regular damage.
    • For example, a Goblin Warlock casts  Armour of Agathys on themselves, and then  Hex5⁠⁠Cold damage from Armour of Agathys in the process. This triggers Hex to deal an additional 1d6⁠⁠Necrotic to Lae'zel, which is then (erroneously) doubled to 2d6⁠⁠Necrotic due to the Critical Hit.
 Hold Monster
  • Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times, requiring a saving throw for each time they are selected.
 Hunger of Hadar
  • The spell mistakenly uses a fixed DC 12 Spell Save instead of the caster's, although this only affects the 2d6⁠⁠Acid damage, as the rest of the spell's effects do not require a saving throw.
  • When upcast to  Level 4 Spell Slot, no sound effect plays when cast upon an enemy.
 Incinerate
  • The in-game tooltip is malformed and fails to mention that the spell costs two  Soul Charges.
 Insect Plague
  • Despite not dealing any ⁠Poison damage, this spell is tagged as a poison DamageType.
  • When first cast on an enemy, the combat log displays the enemy as making two separate saving throw rolls.
  • After the initial cast, subsequent turns of Insect Plague use the Constitution modifier of the caster, not the spellcasting modifier, in order to determine Difficulty Class.
 Keeper's Fee
  • Despite what is shown by the in-game tooltip, it does not inflict  Cursed: Strength.
 Lightning Arrow
  • The hit chance shown in the preview when targeting the spell is for the saving throw rather than the attack roll.
  • If the target fails the initial saving throw, the attack roll always succeeds.
  • The attack roll is not shown in the combat log. If the attacker misses, there is no indication of why the primary 4d8⁠⁠Lightning damage was not applied.
 Luminous Arrow
  • When receiving this ability via Starry Form, this spell is not properly granted with Wisdom as its spellcasting modifier, and instead uses the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired spellcasting class.
  • Due to data inheritance from  Guiding Bolt, Luminous Arrow is incorrectly flagged as a level 1 Evocation Spell. This can lead to unintended interactions with features such as  Tempestuous Magic and  Empowered Evocation, and leaves Luminous Arrow subject to being  Counterspelled.
 Lunar Bulwark
  • Although Selûne's Protection associated with the  Moon Devotion Robe should be activated by  Lunar Bulwark, it is not; the wearer must instead have the regular version of  Mage Armour cast on them for its radiant damage to function.
 Lunar Flare
  • The tooltip reads that this is a level one evocation spell requiring a level two spell slot.
  • The tooltip incorrectly states that two turns of  Guiding Bolt are applied.
 Mage Hand
  • Mage Hand has  Opportunity Attack but cannot use it as it lacks a  Reaction.
Magic Missile (Illithid Arcanist) Magic Missile (Illithid Arcanist)
  • Due to an incomplete list of spell checks,  Shield will not reduce the damage of these magic missiles for the rest of the turn after Shield is used as a reaction.
 Moonbeam
  • Despite being an Evocation spell, Moonbeam does not interact with  Sculpt Spells.
 Moonmote
  • The spell tooltip states that this aura applies only to melee attacks while the condition tooltip states that this aura applies to "attacks". In actuality, it applies to weapon and unarmed attacks, but does not apply to any spells which are also attacks.
 Otiluke's Freezing Sphere (Launch)
  • This variant of the spell lacks the spell flags which would prevent it from being used when  Silenced.
 Produce Flame
  • The damage on the tooltip for Produce Flame is not marked correctly for the increases at level 5 and 10. The tooltip for the throwing action,  Produce Flame: Hurl, is marked correctly, and the damage scales correctly.
  • The version of this Cantrip granted to Asmodeus tieflings uses the character's Wisdom modifier to hurl the flame, rather than Charisma as stated in the  Produce Flame: Hurl tooltip.
 Produce Flame: Hurl
  • The version of this cantrip granted by the Asmodeus tiefling subrace uses the character's Wisdom modifier to hurl the flame, rather than Charisma, like all other racial spells granted to tieflings.
  • For clerics, the tooltip for Produce Flame does not correctly show the damage increases at levels 5 and 10. The tooltip for the throwing action, Produce Flame: Hurl, is marked correctly, and the damage scales correctly.
  • Produce Flame: Hurl only remains available to a character for 99 turns, while  Produce Flame: Dismiss remains available until long rest. After 10 minutes of in-game time, a character is only left with the ability to dismiss the flame and cannot hurl it.
 Protection from Evil and Good
  • Immunity is not provided against  Charm.
  • The immunity to frightened and possession is against any source, not just the listed creature types.
 Protection from Missiles
  • The in-game tooltip on  Cindersnap Reflexes incorrectly says the target is only protected against the next ranged attack. They will be protected by all ranged attacks while the spell is active.
    • Attacks from off-hand Hand Crossbows are not affected by Protection from Missiles.
 Psionic Suggestion: Halt
  • This spell appears to wrongly copy  Command: Grovel instead of  Command: Halt.
 Heat Metal: Reapply Damage
  • Due to a khn scripting error, Heat Metal: Reapply can never cause an enemy to drop their weapon and will always apply Disadvantage.
 Revivify
  • The second selection of this spell can also target a dead character. If this is done, they swap positions and only the originally selected dead or downed character is revived.
 Sacrifice Soul
  •  Silence does not prevent Tska'an from casting this spell despite technically requiring a verbal component.
 Sanctuary
  • Creatures affected by Sanctuary can still be targeted with  Blight,  Chain Lightning, and  Thorn Whip, due to these spells lacking the IsHarmful spell flag. For the same reason, a large number of NPC actions (for example,  Sharp Rock) can target creatures that are affected by Sanctuary.
  • Neutral NPCs (yellow outlined) with Sanctuary can be targeted with attacks.[verify]
 Sanctuary of Loss

 Shadow Blade
  • Having any hireling cast the spell, then adding any item to their inventory, immediately recalling their soul, and then hiring them again, creates a permanent  Shadow Blade in their inventory, which anyone can use. It is then possible to do this again to have two permanent Shadow Blades and dual wield them. If obtained in this manner, the permanent Shadow Blade only uses the spell's base damage, even if it was originally created via upcasting. These permanent Shadow Blades do not properly function with various effects, such as  Battlemage's Power.

  • Due to a coding error, Shield does not grant charges of  Arcane Ward.

  • When provided by an item, Shield does not provide any beneficial effects which would otherwise normally last until the start of the caster's next turn.
 Slow
  • Normally, the targets of Slow must be distinct, but when upcast to level 4, and only level 4, targets can be selected multiple times. For example, two enemies can be targeted three times each forcing them to make three separate saving throws to avoid being slowed. This is due to the level 4 upcasted version lacking the IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities flag.
  • When cast via scroll, Slow requires 6 targets; as enemies cannot be selected twice, and allies are not targetable, this scroll might be difficult to use after the first round.
